narrative.what_i_did:
Opened with the operator's directive 'Fire up and chew a full bite of context.' Ran the four gates and read the prior session's hand-off honest before touching anything. The grounding gate caught the prior narrative slipping on two ground-truth details — it named HomeScreen.tsx as living in src/screens/ and envelopeRoute.ts in src/features/connections/, but both files actually live elsewhere (src/features/wallet-core/HomeScreen.tsx and src/features/transport/envelopeRoute.ts) and HomeScreen is at 797 lines not 798. Those are minor drift but worth flagging because the next-session pointer would have sent the next carpenter on a hunt before finding the real files. The test gate showed one failure on the full-suite run (transport.test.ts line 319, the chat-versus-envelope subscription isolation assertion); the isolated re-run was 24-of-24 clean in 511ms, so it's a timing race in the concurrent full-suite run rather than a regression from any code change. Surfaced a chip naming four options: fix the vouch loop-back routing (named as the recommended option because grounding had revealed it as a real substrate gap with teeth), the Phase D charter-amendment chain, the receiveSelfMembership orgSelfDecl centralization, or the appcommander metadata cleanup. The operator picked the recommended option on one tap.

The substantive finding from grounding was that the loop-back gap the prior carpenter named as 'UI niceness, not a correctness gap' was actually a routing-substrate gap that broke the whole vouch return leg. The envelopeRoute.ts routeFor function classified every self-membership envelope as action self-membership-receive regardless of who was receiving it, which HomeScreen.routeInbox dispatched to acceptSelfMembership — the org-side accept path. That means when a vouching peer cosigned the joiner's self-membership envelope and sent it back through Mycelium, it landed on the joiner's wallet routed to the org acceptance flow which short-circuits because the joiner is not an org (the existing acceptSelfMembership warn-and-return guard catches it silently), but the joiner saw no absorb button and the cosignature never merged into the held copy. The handshake path solves the same shape of problem via signatures.length as a structural discriminator (1-sig means cosign-witness, more means absorb-cosign) but self-memberships cannot use signature-count alone because a 2-sig self-membership could be either a loop-back returning to the joiner OR a fan-out arriving at the org. Receiver-pubkey context is needed to disambiguate. AbsorbCosignModal itself is generic over Attestation — uses envelopeId plus mergeSignatures with no kind-specific logic — so it would handle a cosigned self-membership cleanly the moment routeFor would route the loop-back case there.

The cut delivered in five focused edits. First, envelopeRoute.ts gained an optional second parameter receiverPubkey on routeFor; the self-membership branch checks whether the receiver IS the envelope subject AND the envelope already carries more than the joiner's own signature, and routes to absorb-cosign in that case with a new label 'Absorb vouch' and a hint that names the vouch context. Second, InboxPanel.tsx and ScanEnvelopeModal.tsx — the two production callers of routeFor — destructure identity from useWallet and pass identity.subject as the receiverPubkey. Third, envelopeRoute.test.ts grew from 5 to 8 tests covering the loop-back happy path, the back-compat fall-through when no receiver context is provided, and the org-side cosigned arrival staying correctly routed when the receiver is not the joiner. Fourth, JoinOrgModal.tsx gained the wallet.hold call on the freshly-signed self-membership in the signAndProceed function, gated to only the requires_vouch policy kind (other policies remain ephemeral on the joiner side until the org accepts), so AbsorbCosignModal's envelopeId lookup can locate the held copy when a vouching peer's cosigned return-envelope arrives. Fifth, JoinOrgModal derives a liveSelfMembership memo from holdings on each render so the QR display, the Mycelium send button, and the CosignRequestModal mount all reach for the latest signature-merged version rather than the stale 1-sig copy held in component state. The send-step vouch banner picked up a tone-scaled progress chip (amber when under threshold, emerald when met) reading liveSelfMembership.signatures.length minus one against policy.from_any_member_count; the chip's copy and the collect-vouches button label both flip when the threshold is met so the operator sees a clear 'ready to send' signal rather than having to count cosignatures themselves.

The peer-side vouch-receive surface is the remaining gap on this loop and stays for a future cut. When a vouching peer first receives the joiner's 1-sig envelope to sign on, routeFor still classifies it as self-membership-receive (because the receiver is not the envelope subject), and HomeScreen.routeInbox dispatches to acceptSelfMembership which warns-and-returns silently on the peer's non-org wallet. The peer sees no surface to sign with, which means the joiner can fan their envelope out but no peer can actually do anything with it on the receiving end. Fixing that needs a new InboxRouteAction (vouch-witness or similar) plus a peer-facing 'vouch for this joiner' signing modal that walks the peer through reviewing the joiner's identity, the target org, and whether they personally vouch — different shape than the existing cosign-witness handshake modal because the semantics differ (vouching is an attestation of personal trust, not a cosignature on a multi-party agreement). I deliberately did not roll that into this cut because it is structurally its own surface and would have doubled the chunk size. Naming it explicitly in this narrative so the next carpenter sees the seam. Four gates all green after: typecheck silent, lint silent, 258 of 258 tests passing in 8.21 seconds (no flake on this run), build clean with no bundle-budget overages. JoinOrgModal grew from 616 to 670 lines (over the 400-line soft warn from cut 3, still under the 800-line hard limit by a comfortable margin); envelopeRoute.ts grew from 79 to 109 lines; envelopeRoute.test.ts grew from 95 to 153 lines. The transport and connections manifests both picked up paragraphs naming the loop-back routing fix, the peer-side surface gap left for future work, and the JoinOrgModal extraction candidate (the proof-candidate finders) for whenever the file next needs touching.
narrative.whats_pending:
The peer-side vouch-receive surface is the natural next chunk on the vouch loop. A vouching peer who receives the joiner's 1-sig self-membership envelope via Mycelium currently sees routing to self-membership-receive which acceptSelfMembership warns-and-returns on (peer is not an org). The peer needs a new actionable surface — a 'vouch for this joiner' modal that walks them through reviewing the joiner's identity, the target organization, and whether they personally know and trust this person enough to attach their signature. That requires a new InboxRouteAction (probably named vouch-witness to mirror cosign-witness), a new routing branch in routeFor that fires when the envelope is a 1-sig self-membership and the receiver is neither the joiner nor any org named in the joiner's org_id leaf, a new state-setter pair in HomeScreen.routeInbox, and a new modal component (likely src/features/cosigning/VouchWitnessModal.tsx or src/features/connections/VouchReceiveModal.tsx depending on which feature folder the operator chooses). The signing mechanic is identical to a cosignature — wallet.sign on the existing envelope, send back to the joiner via Mycelium — but the UX framing needs to be different because the peer is attesting personal trust rather than co-authoring an agreement. The progress chip the joiner sees should pick up the returned cosignature automatically once that peer-side surface ships and the loop closes end-to-end.

The JoinOrgModal file is at 670 lines, well under the 800-line hard limit but over the 400-line soft warn (which was already tripped by cut 3 — this cut added 54 lines on top). The natural extraction candidate when JoinOrgModal next needs touching is the two proof-candidate finders findHandshakeProofCandidates and findCredentialProofCandidates plus their helpers describeHandshakePeer / isCredentialAttestation / isRelationshipAttestation; they are pure-logic helpers with no React or wallet context, so they could move cleanly to src/features/connections/joinOrgProofCandidates.ts as a sibling module and would carry a clear unit-test surface (which the inline JoinOrgModal code currently has none of). That would buy back roughly 50 lines and let the modal stay under the soft warn for another two or three feature-touching cuts.

The HomeScreen.tsx ticked back from 798 (prior session's reported count) to 797 (actual — the prior narrative was off by one), so any feature work that touches HomeScreen still needs an extraction planned in the same commit. Natural candidates remain the inbox-routing dispatcher (the routeInbox function plus its six action branches; could move to a sibling hook useInboxDispatch or to a separate src/features/wallet-core/inboxRouting.ts module) or one of the four tab-content renderers. The two other Phase E4 follow-up threads from the prior hand-off are still available: the Phase D charter-amendment chain (multi-session, brief lands in project-memory/foreman-memory/projects/tapit-wallet/briefs/charter-amendment-chain-roadmap.md) and the receiveSelfMembership orgSelfDecl-lookup centralization (small one-session cut). The appcommander metadata cleanup chip is still on the menu pending operator confirmation of whether the AppCommander cockpit polls those files from origin/main.
narrative.what_you_could_do_better:
Two honest observations. First, the receiver-pubkey disambiguation in routeFor uses case-insensitive comparison via toLowerCase on both sides, which matches the convention the rest of the codebase uses for pubkey comparisons (the evaluateJoinPolicy helper, the findHandshakeProofCandidates filter, the verifyOpenJoinedMembership structural gates all do the same). That is the right call for back-compat reasons because some upstream pieces store pubkeys in mixed case. But it is an invariant maintained by convention rather than by type — there is no PubkeyHex newtype that the type system would enforce, so a future caller passing a wallet pubkey from a source that bypassed the convention could silently mismatch. Not worth introducing a newtype just for this routing change, but worth flagging because pubkey-comparison correctness keeps coming up across this codebase and a quiet convention is fragile to drift. If the appcommander-side doctrine wants a pattern note about pubkey comparison hygiene, this would be a reasonable place to suggest it.

Second observation: the JoinOrgModal change wallet.holds the signed self-membership only for the requires_vouch policy kind, on the rationale that other policies do not need the envelope persisted on the joiner side because the org will accept or reject in one round-trip without the joiner needing to do anything else with the envelope. That reasoning is correct for the current cut but creates a small surface inconsistency — if a future feature wants to show the joiner 'here are the join requests you have outstanding,' the non-vouch policies will not have entries in holdings to render. The honest answer is probably to wallet.hold on every policy kind once the joiner signs (then the JoinOrgModal becomes the surface for the joiner to track their pending join requests), but that is a separate UX question about whether outstanding joins are operator-visible state. I made the narrow choice here to keep the cut chunk-shaped, and named it in the manifest note so the next carpenter can see the seam. The cost of the narrow choice is that operator-discoverability of 'what join requests am I waiting on' is bounded by what JoinOrgModal happens to be showing right now; the cost of the wider choice would have been growing this cut beyond the chunk size and introducing a UI surface that has no place to live yet.
narrative.bigger_picture:
Loop closure is the deeper teaching moment of this cut. The prior session shipped the joiner-side ability to fan a signed self-membership out to vouching peers, which was a forward-direction substrate cut — the joiner can now call CosignRequestModal in org_vouch mode and reach N peers through Mycelium. But every multi-party signing flow has a return leg, and a return leg without an absorb surface is a fan-out that goes nowhere. The CosignRequestModal fan-out plus the AbsorbCosignModal absorb are two halves of the same multi-party-signing primitive; the prior session shipped the forward half and named the return half as polish, but the return half is structurally part of what makes the forward half worth shipping at all. A wallet that can ASK for vouches but cannot RECEIVE them is a wallet with a button that does nothing useful. The substrate gap I found and closed was the routing fix that makes the AbsorbCosignModal accessible to the joiner when a returned cosigned envelope arrives; the JoinOrgModal liveSelfMembership and progress chip closed the operator-visibility side so the joiner can see the vouches accumulating as they come back.

The deeper pattern this cut surfaces is that routing primitives that take only the envelope (no receiver context) work for kinds where the envelope's shape carries enough information to dispatch unambiguously — handshakes (signature count discriminates), org-issued memberships (kind alone discriminates), recovery shares (kind alone discriminates). They start to break for kinds where the same envelope can flow through multiple network positions with different correct actions at each position. Self-memberships are the first kind in this codebase that has that property: a single envelope can legitimately arrive at three different wallets (joiner-on-loop-back, vouching-peer, org) with three different correct dispatches. The fix pattern here — pass the receiver pubkey through, do the disambiguation only for the kind that needs it, leave the back-compat fall-through for callers that have not been wired yet — is a clean way to handle that without re-architecting the whole routing layer. If future kinds emerge with similar multi-position semantics (and they will — the charter-amendment chain the operator has on the roadmap will probably have similar properties, where an amendment envelope can flow through proposer, voter, and ratifier positions), the same receiver-aware-routing pattern extends cleanly. The discriminated-union pattern the prior session named for the CosignRequestModal orgContext prop has a routing-layer cousin in this cut: there too, a single primitive (routeFor) absorbs variation by taking a small amount of context rather than fragmenting into siblings.

The Layer 2 to Layer 4 ladder the prior session named is exactly the ladder this cut climbs one more rung on. The vouch fan-out + absorb together are a Layer 2 multi-party signing mechanism. The JoinOrgModal progress chip and the autoroute-to-absorb behavior are the Layer 4 frictionless surface that lets the joiner participate in that mechanism without having to think about the routing, the merge, or the cosignature count. A wallet that holds keys and signs is Layer 1; a wallet that lets another party request a signature and route the response is Layer 2; a wallet where the joiner taps 'Collect vouch' and watches the progress chip tick up as peers respond is Layer 4 — and crucially, every layer above Layer 1 is built from primitives that already exist in the wallet, composed rather than re-implemented. This cut composed three existing primitives (routeFor, AbsorbCosignModal's mergeSignatures, JoinOrgModal's existing CosignRequestModal mount) plus one tiny new piece (the receiver-aware self-membership branch) into a closed loop. That ratio of composition to invention is what makes the layer-climbing feel manageable rather than overwhelming.

feedback_to_appcommander: Two patterns worth lifting into the AppCommander-side doctrine. First, the receiver-aware-routing pattern: routing primitives that dispatch from envelope shape alone work for kinds where shape is unambiguous, but kinds whose envelopes can legitimately arrive at multiple network positions with different correct actions need receiver context passed through. The fix pattern is to add an optional receiver parameter with back-compat fall-through behavior when omitted, do the disambiguation only inside the kind branch that needs it, and update callers incrementally. That pattern will extend cleanly to future multi-position envelope kinds (the operator's roadmap'd charter-amendment chain will probably need it). Second, the prior session's narrative correctly named the discriminated-union pattern for absorbing variation into a single prop; this session showed the same pattern applies one layer down at the routing level. Both are 'absorb variation into a small amount of context rather than fragmenting into siblings.' Worth a doctrine note about composability and the threshold for adding a context parameter versus splitting a primitive.
